findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level, dumping full ID lists
findings.body: Each batch in the cleanup loops logs at Error level, including the full slice of IDs, at lines 534/537, 554/557 and 576/579. This happens even on success and even when there are zero IDs. With large batch sizes (e.g. 32767) every cleanup cycle emits enormous error-level log lines. That floods logs and triggers false alerts. These look like leftover debugging and should be removed or lowered to Debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker was reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which looks like a debugging leftover unrelated to the deadlock fix. All cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, query history, etc.) now run 10x more often, increasing DB load. The per-run timeout is still 9 minutes, so runs can overlap or queue behind each other. That also increases contention with the very writes this PR aims to stop deadlocking.

findings.title: SQLite inline-ID path is quadratic
findings.body: On SQLite with a large batch size, the IN list is built by calling fmt.Sprintf repeatedly on a growing string. That is O(n^2) in the number of IDs, which is expensive for batches of ~32k. A strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt (as used elsewhere in this file) should be used instead.

findings.title: MaxCount loop can delete annotations inserted concurrently
findings.body: The MaxCount pass fetches IDs with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT batch OFFSET maxCount and loops until nothing is deleted. Because the fetch and the delete are now separate statements, and repeated without a transaction, concurrent inserts shift the offset window between iterations. The loop keeps going while new rows arrive, so it can run for a long time under steady insert load.
